decisions.reason: After two years the evening psychiatric day-patient program has shown enough persistence to justify keeping it, as it is strongly aligned with our psychiatric services even if specialist staffing remains costly.
The carpentry workshop still fits our sheltered-workshop and training capabilities, and its continued presence supports keeping the option open despite meaningful market and cost risk.
The counseling service for senior living is highly consistent with our eldercare expertise, low-cost to maintain, and strategically useful as a feeder into related services.
The retail shop is still the most peripheral and operationally vulnerable option, and by now the expected value of continuing in consumer retail no longer outweighs the resources it ties up.
Meal delivery for seniors is close to our core offer and deserves more time to test demand and routing economics, though its logistics-heavy model keeps withdrawal risk moderate.
